_about: THE SAMPLE PROJECT — Dragon, a feature.
READ THIS FIRST. Everything in this file that looks like production
paperwork is INVENTED. The schedule, the shoot dates, the budget, the
unit list, the call sheets, the recce notes, the shot list, the boards
and the script pages are a TEACHING RECONSTRUCTION, written for this
app so that every downstream module has something real to render. They
are not this production's documents and no part of them was taken from
the production. A sample that lies about its own nature teaches the
wrong thing, so it says what it is here, in meta_started, in the
writer field, on the first call sheet and in every document body.
WHAT IS TRUE. The film is real: Dragon (2025), directed by Ashwath
Marimuthu, in Tamil, produced by AGS Entertainment. The premise, the
logline, the character spine and the fifteen beats are condensed from
src/data/studies.json's own Dragon case study — craft analysis this
project already wrote and vetted — rather than invented a second time
or imported from somewhere else.
NO REAL PERSON IS GIVEN INVENTED CONTACT DETAILS. Every name in the
`contacts` list is invented, with a +91 90000 1xxxx number and a
@dragon.example address — `.example` is a reserved TLD and can never
route. The `role` column carries CHARACTER names, which are public.
The one real person named anywhere in the paperwork is the director,
in the Director field and the HOD sheet's director row, because that
is a credit and not an assignment; his sign-off date is deliberately
left blank, since inventing a signature for a real person is the
thing this rule exists to prevent. Every other HOD row is an
invented stand-in.
NO REPRODUCTION OF THE FILM'S SCREENPLAY — which is a narrower claim
than this paragraph used to make. It said there was no dialogue
anywhere in the sample, and that was true for as long as the script
pages were seven headings and some action. They are a full 36-scene
screenplay now, in sample.dragon.script.json, because a writing tool
whose demo project has no script cannot show the Write module, the
screenplay PDF, the sides, the page count or the AI shot division
doing anything at all — and because the scene rows below claimed 105
pages while the script held 2.3, which is the sample contradicting
itself about the one number everything else here is derived from.
Every line of those pages is ORIGINAL, written for this app from the
synopses below and from the character fields in `blueprint`, and from
nothing else. None of it is Ashwath Marimuthu's dialogue — not quoted,
not recalled, not approximated — and the first two elements on the
page say so, because the Write module is where somebody will actually
read them.
THE DIALOGUE IS TANGLISH; the slug lines, action and transitions are
English. That is what a Tamil unit shoots from, and it is the only
arrangement in which the page count stays arithmetic — see that
file's own note, which also explains why it is romanised rather than
Tamil script, and why `--f-script` would punish the other choice.
studies.json's rule still holds for the part it was written about.
Each `synopsis` here is the one functional line a 1st AD writes, never
a narrative beat, so these 36 rows remain a PRODUCTION document: slug
line, INT/EXT, day/night, location, eighths, page, shoot day and the
elements in the scene.
The 36 scenes are a CONDENSED reconstruction at 105 pages, and the
screenplay is written to that figure scene by scene rather than
allowed to drift from it — see that file's own note for how, and for
why it is a dynamic import. The finished film runs 155 minutes and its
real breakdown is much longer; this one is sized to teach the modules,
not to stand in for a script.
ONE sample, in ONE file. It used to be two: a four-scene 'Sample —
Dragon' seeded by the hub's first-run panel, and a separate Por
Thozhil field dump embedded in src/pages/feature.js and fetched from
a root JSON file. Two samples meant two answers to 'what does a
filled studio look like', and the short one could not fill a single
downstream module.
Everything the hub seeds is here and nowhere else — invariant 2. The
hub reads this file and writes it through the same models the app
reads: src/lib/scenes.js, contacts.js, locations.js, shots.js,
script.js, and the estimator's own ci_<n>_* field shape. No second
representation:
* scene ids are DERIVED from the scene number ('dragon-sc-<number>'),
so a shot, a call sheet or a frame refers to a scene by NUMBER here
and the hub resolves it once. Nothing in this file writes an id
twice.
* shoot days, locations, cast and page counts are NOT listed anywhere.
They are what the scene rows already say, and the stripboard, day
out of days, calendar and budget all read them back off the scenes.
* the blueprint's own legacy tables (sl_*, cast_*, loc_*, shot_*) are
deliberately left EMPTY. Filling them would be the scene list stored
a second time, which is the stranded-key trap CLAUDE.md names.
* v2s11_days and v2s11_pages are filled by the hub FROM the scenes, not
typed here, so the paperwork cannot disagree with the schedule.
PHASES 03 AND 04 ARE EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and the reason is not that the
film was never shot — it was shot, and it released on 21 February
2025. The reason is that this package is a snapshot taken at ONE
moment: the week before an invented first day, draft locked, recce
done, two locations still waiting on written permission. Ticking the
production and post checklists would describe a shoot that nothing
else in this file documents, and the progress numbers would stop
meaning anything. The empty phases are the snapshot's date, not a
claim about the film.
The rate figures in the estimator come from src/data/rates.chennai.*
unchanged. No rate here was invented and no inflation multiplier was
applied — see CLAUDE.md open item 7 for why that matters.
title: Dragon

blueprint.meta_writer: Sample reconstruction · the film is Ashwath Marimuthu's (2025)
blueprint.meta_started: Sample data · invented paperwork for a real film
blueprint.v2_budget: ₹ 4.6 crore all-in — sample estimate, not the production's figure
blueprint.s1_whatif: What if the life you talked your way into could only be kept by going back and actually earning it?
blueprint.s1_why_me: Because the film lets the audience enjoy the shortcut for an hour and then hands them the invoice at the same moment it hands one to him. That is a structure worth taking apart, which is why it is the sample.
blueprint.s1_image: A boy collecting a medal he genuinely earned, in 2014, in a hall of plastic chairs — and the same man, years later, earning something much smaller and keeping it.
blueprint.s2_log1: A young man living on a forged degree is recognised by the one person who can prove it.
blueprint.s2_log2: A college dropout who talked his way into a corporate career on a forged degree is given one term by his former dean to clear the papers he never passed.
blueprint.s2_log_final: A young man living on a forged degree is recognised by his former dean and given one term to clear the papers he never passed, or lose the job, the engagement and the last person still willing to believe him.
blueprint.s3_theme: A result nobody audits is still not the same thing as having done the work.
blueprint.s3_ext: Can he clear every arrear inside the dean's deadline without either of his two lives discovering the other?
blueprint.s3_int: Can he become someone worth believing, rather than someone good at being believed?
blueprint.s3_phil: Is a competence that is real made honest by a credential that is not?
blueprint.s4_arc: From a boy who buys the outcome to a man who chooses the loss that buys the truth.
blueprint.s4_want: Status large enough to be seen by the people who wrote him off.
blueprint.s4_lie: The result is the only thing anybody ever audits.
blueprint.s4_wound: He was turned down for the exact quality the film had just spent ten minutes establishing as a virtue.
blueprint.s4_skill: He can be believed by anyone in under a minute.
blueprint.s4_flaw: He has never tested whether he is worth believing.
blueprint.s5_want: The rule applied without exception to the one student who proved it could be ignored.
blueprint.s5_philosophy: A rule that bends for the person who most wants it bent is not a rule.
blueprint.s5_hero: He is simply correct, and he is never cruel. There is nothing in his position to push against, which is what forces the protagonist to do the work himself.
blueprint.s5_mirror: He cannot tell the difference between enforcing a rule and being right about a person; the protagonist cannot tell the difference between a result and the work behind it. Both are reading one number and calling it a judgement.
blueprint.s5_humanity: He keeps whatever yield he has for the latest possible moment, so when it comes it reads as earned rather than granted.
blueprint.s6_ally_reflect: He is the version of the protagonist who never had to be believed by anyone.
blueprint.s6_ally_subplot: He keeps the count the protagonist refuses to keep.
blueprint.s6_ally_exit: He is the one asked for the help that turns the second act into a debt.
blueprint.s6_lover_sees: That nothing has been decided about what he intends to become.
blueprint.s6_lover_goal: To get an answer to the question, rather than a performance of one.
blueprint.s6_lover_decision: She asks it once more and does not take the performance.
blueprint.s6_mentor_tool: He is the price of the shortcut, in a currency the audience can read.
blueprint.s6_mentor_failure: He absorbed a cost that was not his and never billed it to anyone.
blueprint.s7_location: Chennai — an engineering campus, a corporate floor, Villivakkam, Parrys Corner, Besant Nagar
blueprint.s7_duration: One academic term, against the dean's three-month deadline
blueprint.s7_rules: 1. The comedy and the drama are about the SAME subject, never alternating blocks. 2. The antagonist is correct and never cruel. 3. The competence is real; only the credential is forged. 4. The consequence is filmed, not skipped in a cut. 5. The last image is smaller than the first and worth more.
blueprint.s7_sensory: Corridor fluorescence, a notice board behind glass, a corporate floor with no shadows in it. A number read aloud twice — once for a laugh and once as a workload.
blueprint.s9_chrono: 2014 prize day → the rejection → college and the arrears → the forged certificate → the job → recognition → the ultimatum → the attempt → the harm → the confession → the sentence → the delivery route.
blueprint.s9_screen: Chronological, with the opening image doing the structural work: the audience sees merit that was genuinely earned before it ever sees a shortcut, so the fall is a tragedy rather than a diagnosis.
blueprint.s9_why: The film asks the audience to like the con for an hour. That only works if the order is honest — enjoy it first, pay for it second, and never be told in advance which jokes are evidence.
blueprint.s10_setup_1: A number used as comic shorthand, repeatedly, in the first half.
blueprint.s10_pay_1: The same number read back as a workload with a deadline on it.
blueprint.s10_setup_2: The plan stated out loud and in full in act one.
blueprint.s10_pay_2: Every later compromise is measurable against it without a line of dialogue.
blueprint.s10_setup_3: A rejection delivered for a quality the set-up had just established as a virtue.
blueprint.s10_pay_3: The whole film is the rebuttal of that one stated reason.
blueprint.s10_setup_4: The B story asks what he intends to become.
blueprint.s10_pay_4: The antagonist asks the same question with authority behind it.
blueprint.s10_setup_5: An opening image of merit actually earned.
blueprint.s10_pay_5: A final image of merit rebuilt from nothing, smaller and worth more.
blueprint.b01: 2014 prize day. A medal that was genuinely earned, before the film shows a single shortcut.
blueprint.b02: The theme stated as its own inversion — he is turned down for the quality the picture will spend itself defending.
blueprint.b03: The whole plan said out loud: engineering, a masters abroad, then marriage.
blueprint.b04: The rejection. Personal rather than academic, and precise about the insult.
blueprint.b05: Almost no debate at all. The missing deliberation is the characterisation.
blueprint.b06: He becomes Dragon. The act-two choice is an identity, not a plan.
blueprint.b07: The college relationship carries the argument while the A story is busy being funny.
blueprint.b08: Notoriety, played broad, and the arrears accumulating as a running joke.
blueprint.b09: A false victory: the credential is fake and the competence is real, which is what makes the rest an argument.
blueprint.b10: Promotion, a proposal, and the one man holding the document that undoes all of it. Three months on the clock.
blueprint.b11: Not the exposure — the harm. The cost lands on somebody who never took the shortcut.
blueprint.b12: Guilt carried quietly against a date that is still fixed. The comedy stops; that is how the beat is marked.
blueprint.b13: He is offered a clean way out and declines it.
blueprint.b14: Confession, surrender, and the sentence filmed rather than skipped.
blueprint.b15: A smaller life, presented as sufficient rather than as a punishment.
blueprint.s12_note_v1: Decide now which of the first act's laughs will be re-read in the third, and plant each one twice. Do not let the comedy and the drama end up being about two different subjects.
blueprint.v2s1_draft: Reconstruction draft — 36 scenes, 105 pages, condensed for the sample. Locked 2 Feb 2024 (invented).
blueprint.v2s1_weak: 1. Two canteen scenes are doing one job. 2. The dean states the rule twice; the second time is a reminder, not a scene. 3. The corporate floor is written with more extras than a built set can hold.
blueprint.v2s1_signoff: Invented sign-off, for the sample: producer, DOP and editor on 4 Feb 2024. The director's row on the HOD sheet carries a real credit and no date — see _about.
blueprint.v2s2_theme: A result nobody audits is still not the same thing as having done the work.
blueprint.v2s2_tone1: Broad and warm for an hour, then quiet. Two tones on one subject, never in alternating blocks.
blueprint.v2s2_tone2: Funny · fast · specific · unsparing in the last reel
blueprint.v2s2_refs: Nanban for the campus register and 3 Idiots for the arrears as comedy; Aruvi for the point at which a comic picture stops being one.
blueprint.v2s2_refuse: No montage that skips the sentence. No reprieve and no technicality. No villain who is wrong. No slow-motion entry for the new name. No scene where the comedy is about something the drama is not.
blueprint.v2s2_para: Everything we build exists so the audience can enjoy the con without reservation for an hour. That means the campus is funny and the corporate floor is flattering, and neither is shot ironically. When the register changes in the last reel, nothing in the design changes with it — the audience's understanding is what moved.
blueprint.v2s3_palette: Corporate blue-grey, campus ochre, notice-board cream
blueprint.v2s3_light: Hard corridor fluorescence on campus, and a corporate floor with no shadows anywhere in it — the flattery is in the lighting. The last reel takes the fill out and nothing else.
blueprint.v2s3_frames: The campus is handheld and loose. The office is locked off and symmetrical. The dean's office is always from the student's chair.
blueprint.v2s3_texture: Glass over a notice board, laminate, lanyards, a printed certificate that will be held to a desk lamp and read.
blueprint.v2s5_speciallens: 100mm macro on the truck every day, for the certificate and the mark sheets
blueprint.v2s5_light_phil: Flatter the corporate floor and do not flatter the campus. Capture is 4.6K open gate, ProRes 4444, delivered 4K DCI.
blueprint.v2s5_grade: Clean and bright through the first two acts so the last reel can simply stop being either.
blueprint.v2s6_sets: Dean's office (built), corporate open floor and glass meeting room (built, same floor), everything else location.
blueprint.v2s6_dressed: The arrears notice board is a continuity spine — three states, and the audience is meant to read it each time.
blueprint.v2s6_heroprops: The forged degree certificate. Three copies: hero, insert and one aged for the last reel.
blueprint.v2s6_recurring: Lanyard, mark sheet, the notice board behind glass.
blueprint.v2s6_period: 2014 prologue: school banner with the year on it, no smartphones in the hall, period two-wheelers on the street.
blueprint.v2s7_protag: Three stages, one silhouette: a school uniform, four years of campus clothes that get louder, and a corporate shirt that fits too well.
blueprint.v2s7_antag: One jacket, worn in every scene, never once adjusted.
blueprint.v2s7_period: 2014: school uniform, canvas shoes, no branding anywhere in the hall.
blueprint.v2s10_bgm: Fourteen cues, 31 minutes. Score carries the comedy for two acts and then withdraws entirely for the last reel — the silence is how the beat is marked.
blueprint.v2s10_refs: A light campus palette for the first hour; nothing at all under the confession.
blueprint.v2s10_phil: The dean's office has no music in it, ever. Mix is four days at a Chennai studio (sample).
blueprint.v2s11_blocks: Three blocks: campus location (days 1–6, a vacation window), built sets — dean's office and corporate floor (days 7–12), Chennai locations and the last reel (days 13–18).
blueprint.v2s11_expday: Day 14 — marriage hall, 300 background, one unit, no second camera.
blueprint.v2s11_largest: Camera and lighting package, 18 days, plus the built corporate floor.
blueprint.v2s12_recce: 5–7 Feb 2024 (invented) — engineering campus, the two built sets, Parrys print lane, Villivakkam house, Virugambakkam marriage hall, Besant Nagar beach road.
blueprint.v2s12_problems: 1. The campus is only available in a six-day vacation window. 2. The arrears board has to be legible on a 100mm macro and is behind glass. 3. Parrys print lane trades from 09:30 and will not close. 4. The marriage hall is a Sunday and 300 background. 5. Besant Nagar beach road has a 28-minute dusk.
blueprint.v2s12_resolutions: 1. Six consecutive campus days, no returns — 1st AD Nivetha owns the window. 2. Polariser plus a dulling spray on the glass, DOP Hari tested on 6 Feb. 3. Shoot the lane 06:00–09:00, one day. 4. Two assistant directors on background and a 05:00 dressing call. 5. Two dusk passes budgeted, not one.
blueprint.v2s12_note: Shoot the opening medal before anything else. Everything after it is measured against it.
blueprint.p3_base: Campus car park, then the Madhavaram floor
blueprint.lad_1_logline: A young man living on a forged degree is recognised by his former dean and given one term to clear the papers he never passed, or lose the job, the engagement and the last person still willing to believe him.
blueprint.lad_2_synopsis: A brilliant school student is turned down for a college seat — not on his marks, but on the kind of person he appears to be. He converts the humiliation straight into a new identity, accumulates a notorious college career and the arrears that go with it, and walks into a corporate job on a certificate he did not earn. He is genuinely good at the work, which is what turns the rest of the film into an argument rather than a lecture. Then the one man who knows what he is recognises him, and hands him a deadline instead of an exposure.
blueprint.lad_3_onepager: Genre: drama / character study. Length: 105 pages / 36 scenes (condensed reconstruction). Budget: ₹4.6 cr (sample estimate). Schedule: 18 days, Chennai. The hook is that the audience is made complicit in the con for an hour and then handed the invoice at the same moment the protagonist is.
blueprint.lad_5_outline: Fifteen beats, in Vol I step 11, condensed from the Save the Cat sheet in src/data/studies.json.

scenes.synopsis: 2014 prize day. Young Ragavan collects the medal; parents at the back of the hall.

special: Scissor lift for the high wide

scenes.synopsis: 2014. The plan stated out loud at the gate — engineering, masters, marriage.
Ragavan arrives on campus three years in and treats the front block as his own.
The arrears board. Ragavan counts his own list in front of an audience.
Canteen. Ragavan runs the room; Anbu keeps the score he refuses to keep.
Quad. The notoriety established — known by everybody, known for nothing.
First summons. The rule is stated and not negotiated.

sound: Room tone only — no music cue

scenes.synopsis: Hostel, night. Anbu reads out what is left to clear.
Canteen. Keerthi asks the question the film will keep asking.
Quad, dusk. Keerthi leaves the conversation open. Magic-hour, two passes.
Exam hall. One paper attempted, badly. Full invigilation unit.
The board again. The number has gone up. Macro insert, continuity-critical.
Hostel, night. The name is adopted. Haircut and wardrobe change on camera.

special: Second camera for the single-take change

scenes.synopsis: The certificate is ordered. Insert-heavy, hands and paper.
Ragavan talks his way past the HR desk.
First day on the floor; he is good at it immediately. Establishing wide plus coverage.
Six months on. Promotion board and a desk move.
House, night. The father is told a version of events.
The client pitch he carries alone. Locked off, symmetrical.
Beach road, dusk. Pallavi and the proposal. Two dusk passes budgeted.
A campus visit he did not plan. The dean recognises him.
The ultimatum: one term, every arrear. The longest two-hander in the film.

sound: Room tone only — no music cue

scenes.synopsis: Re-admission formalities, done in public. Crowd reaction unit.
Two lives run at once; the first slip. Night floor, skeleton background.

props: Mark sheets in a laptop bag
special: Practical desk lamps carry the scene

scenes.synopsis: The board, a third time — his own name, current. Macro insert.
The attempt, properly. Full invigilation unit, longest set-up count of the shoot.
Anbu is asked for help and sets a price.
The answer-sheet swap. Two sittings, continuity-critical; insert unit on the booklets.
The engagement date is fixed in the office. Background-heavy.
The classmate's offer is lost. Minimal unit, no background, one source.
The result, and what it cost somebody else.

sound: Room tone only — no music cue

scenes.synopsis: Ragavan stops arguing. Score out from here to the end of the reel.
The decision made at home, without a speech.
The confession, in front of 300 background. One unit, no second camera.
Surrender and sentence. Procedural, no music, no coverage of reactions.
Delivery route. Final image; one unit, available light, long lens from the car.

special: Long lens from the camera car, no track

Engineering college — front block.address: Campus main gate and front block, Tambaram
Engineering college — front block.contact: College administrative office — Mr K. Rajendran
Engineering college — front block.power: Campus supply at the front block, 63A three phase
Engineering college — front block.toilets: Block A facility, open for the unit
Engineering college — front block.bestTime: 06:30–17:00. Six consecutive days only — the vacation window, with no returns.
Engineering college — front block.cost: ₹ 55,000 per day, six days agreed (sample figure)
Engineering college — front block.notes: The whole campus is one permission and one window. If a day slips here it cannot be made up, so the two exterior days are first and the interiors follow.

Engineering college — quad.contact: College administrative office — Mr K. Rajendran
Engineering college — quad.power: Quad supply, 32A. Genny for the night unit.
Engineering college — quad.parking: Staff car park, 400m from the quad
Engineering college — quad.bestTime: Day unit 07:00–16:00. Dusk window is 26 minutes and needs two passes.
Engineering college — quad.notes: The night scene has no background and one HMI through the trees — the smallest unit of the shoot, scheduled on its own day so it cannot eat a crowd day.

Dean's office.bestTime: Any. Three scenes, all day interior.
Dean's office.notes: Built with a removable fourth wall so both 50mm cameras can sit in the student's chair line. No music is ever cut into this set, so the sound department shoots it clean.

Corporate office — open floor.bestTime: Any. Blacked out for the night floor scene.
Corporate office — open floor.notes: Fifty-five dressed workstations, which is the ceiling — the script asks for more in two scenes and the 1st AD has re-blocked both. 30ft of track runs the length of the aisle.

Certificate print lane, Parrys Corner.address: Print and stationery lane off NSC Bose Road, Parrys Corner
Certificate print lane, Parrys Corner.power: Shop supply only, 15A. Battery lighting for the insert table.
Certificate print lane, Parrys Corner.parking: None in the lane. Unit vehicles on NSC Bose Road, 250m walk.
Certificate print lane, Parrys Corner.bestTime: 06:00–09:00. The lane trades from 09:30 and will not close.
Certificate print lane, Parrys Corner.notes: Permission is verbal as of the recce. Production executive chasing the written one — do not lock the date until it lands.

Ragavan's house, Villivakkam.power: House supply, 15A. One 30 KVA genny on the street.
Ragavan's house, Villivakkam.parking: Street parking, 8 vehicles, with a traffic constable booked
Ragavan's house, Villivakkam.bestTime: Any. The 2014 exterior wants morning light on the gate.
Ragavan's house, Villivakkam.cost: ₹ 40,000 per day, two days agreed (sample figure)
Ragavan's house, Villivakkam.notes: One address carries both periods. Period dressing goes up at 05:00 for the 2014 exterior and comes down before the present-day interiors, so the order within the day is fixed.

Marriage hall, Virugambakkam.bestTime: Sunday only. 05:00 dressing call, 300 background from 08:00.
Marriage hall, Virugambakkam.cost: ₹ 1,10,000 for the day plus background catering (sample figure)
Marriage hall, Virugambakkam.notes: The biggest day in the film and the only one with 300 people on it. Two ADs on background, one unit, no second camera — a second camera here costs more in holding than it saves in coverage.

Besant Nagar beach road.bestTime: Dusk. 28 minutes of the light we want, so two passes are budgeted, not one.
Besant Nagar beach road.notes: Public road and a public crowd — crowd control is the whole problem here, not light. If the permission does not land, the scene moves to the campus quad at dusk and loses nothing structural.

shots.description: Crane down over the front block, finding him in a crowd that already knows him. One take, before the 08:00 class change.
Travel with him through the crowd. Every greeting arrives from off-frame.
Anbu keeping up and half a step behind, which is where he stays for two acts.
The front block held two beats after he leaves frame. Establishes the place the last reel comes back to.
The floor entire, locked off and symmetrical. No shadows anywhere — the flattery is in the lighting.
Dolly the length of the aisle on 30ft of track, matching his walking pace exactly.
He is good at the work. Play it straight and give it the same coverage a competent person would get.
The lanyard and the printed name. Legible — the audience reads it with him.
Sixty candidates from the back of the hall, one clock in frame. The clock is the scene.
His desk, straight on. No handheld in this hall at all.
The booklet number. Insert table, and it has to match the swap two scenes later.
The classmate four desks away, working, unaware he is in the film's most expensive scene.
The hall and 300 people in it, from the gallery. One take at 08:30 while the background is still fresh.
Through the guests to the stage. The only handheld in the last reel.
Held, long, with nothing cut under it. The score is already out by this point.
The hall after. Background holds position; nobody is directed to react.

documents.title: Dragon — sample treatment (reconstruction)
documents.body:
SAMPLE DOCUMENT. This is a reconstruction written for the sample project. The film — Dragon (2025), directed by Ashwath Marimuthu — is real; this treatment is not the production's, and nothing in it was taken from the production. It stays at the level of premise, structure and craft, because a scene-by-scene account of a film is both a worse lesson and not ours to publish.

PREMISE. A college dropout who talked his way into a corporate career on a forged degree is recognised by the one man who can prove it, and can only keep the life he invented by going back and actually earning it.

THE HOOK. The shortcut is charming and the bill is not. The audience is made complicit in the con for an hour, then handed the invoice at the same moment the protagonist is.

HOW IT IS BUILT. The opening movement plays as comedy and lets the audience enjoy the protagonist's nerve without reservation. The forged credential is introduced as a joke and the count of unfinished papers runs as a gag, so when both are re-read as arithmetic the tonal shift arrives as a consequence rather than as a change of genre.

THE ANTAGONIST IS CORRECT. The opposing character holds a position the audience cannot dismiss and a manner that offers nothing to push against. Malice can be defeated; a correct rule has to be satisfied, and satisfying it is the only thing that makes the protagonist do the work himself.

WHERE THE COST LANDS. The low point is an accounting rather than an exposure — the bill arrives in a form that cannot be argued with, and it was paid by somebody who never took the shortcut. The climax is therefore a choice the protagonist could have avoided, which is the only kind of confession that proves anything.

THE ENDING. The new life is smaller than the invented one and better founded, and it is presented as sufficient rather than as a punishment. That is what keeps the film an argument instead of a warning.

FOR THIS SAMPLE: 105 pages, 36 scenes, 18 days. All three figures are invented and condensed; the finished film runs 155 minutes.

documents.title: Approach note — written for the sample, not by the film's director
documents.body:
SAMPLE DOCUMENT. Nobody connected with Dragon wrote this. It exists so the Write module has a director's statement to show, and so a filmmaker reading the sample can see what one is for.

The discipline of this reconstruction is that the comedy and the drama are about the SAME subject. Tonal shifts break a film when the two tones are about different things; sharing a subject makes the shift read as the audience's understanding deepening rather than as the film losing its nerve. So nothing is shot ironically in the first hour — the campus is funny and the corporate floor is flattering, and the design does not change when the register does.

That one rule decides the lenses (a 100mm macro is on the truck every day, because the audience has to read the notice board, the mark sheets and the certificate at the same moment the characters do), the lighting (hard corridor fluorescence on campus, a floor with no shadow in it at the office, and the fill simply taken out in the last reel), and the blocking (the dean's office is always from the student's chair).

What this approach refuses: a montage that skips the sentence, a reprieve, a technicality, a slow-motion entry for the new name, and a villain who is wrong. If the theme is consequence, the consequence gets filmed.

documents.title: One-pager — for the market (sample)
documents.body:
DRAGON — SAMPLE RECONSTRUCTION
Drama / character study · Tamil · 105 pages · 18 shoot days · ₹4.6 cr

EVERY FIGURE ON THIS PAGE IS INVENTED. The film is real — Dragon (2025), directed by Ashwath Marimuthu, produced by AGS Entertainment — and this is a teaching package built around it, not its paperwork.

LOGLINE
A young man living on a forged degree is recognised by his former dean and given one term to clear the papers he never passed, or lose the job, the engagement and the last person still willing to believe him.

WHY NOW
A credential economy, and a generation that has watched the result be the only thing anybody audits. The film has no villain who is wrong.

SHAPE
Comedy for an hour, then the invoice. Two tones on one subject, never in alternating blocks.

PACKAGE (invented stand-ins)
DOP Hari Shankar · Editor Praveen Antony · PD Meera Raghavan · 1st AD Nivetha Balan · Producer Bhuvana Sekar.

STATUS (invented)
Reconstruction draft locked 2 Feb 2024. Recce complete. Floor from 12 Feb 2024. Two locations pending written permission.

documents.title: Character bible — Ragavan (sample)
documents.body:
SAMPLE DOCUMENT. Condensed from the Dragon case study in src/data/studies.json — craft analysis, not a plot account.

RAGAVAN, called 'Dragon'. A young man whose one real talent is being believed, and who has never tested whether he is worth believing.

WANT: status large enough to be seen by the people who wrote him off.
NEED: self-respect he did not manufacture.
LIE: the result is the only thing anybody ever audits.
WOUND: he was turned down for the exact quality the first act had just established as a virtue. The rejection was personal, not academic, and the film spends itself proving that reason wrong.
SKILL: he can be believed by anyone in under a minute.
FLAW: he mistakes a result for the work behind it.

EXTERNAL STAKE: career, marriage and standing dissolve together, because they were all built on the same document.
INTERNAL STAKE: he becomes permanently a man who can only be liked by people who do not know him.

ARC: from a boy who buys the outcome to a man who chooses the loss that buys the truth.

WHY THE ACT-TWO CHOICE IS AN IDENTITY AND NOT A PLAN: he does not decide to do anything in particular, he decides to be someone else, and everything that follows arrives as consequence rather than as scheme. That is harder to write and better to watch.

WHY THE LIE IS UNNECESSARY: the competence is real and only the credential is forged. Because he could have done it honestly, the audience argues with itself for the rest of the film instead of being lectured.
